newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT--Dollar/mark set to revisit Feb '94 highs.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT--Dollar/mark set to revisit Feb '94 highs.

text.p: The U.S. dollar, still buoyed by a global rush into U.S. financial assets, is set to revisit levels not seen since February 1994, analysts said on Friday.
The Dow Jones vaulted to another record on Friday and the 30-year Treasury bond yield broke the 6.75-percent barrier.
"Definitely, I think the dollar is going to go higher versus the mark," said Merrill Lynch analyst David Horner, noting that dollar/mark easily took out 1.7330 resistance.
Chartists said the move was significant because it was launched from 1.7270, the 61.8-percent retracement of the fall from 1.7423, the high of June 6, to 1.7020, the low on Monday.
The dollar ended on Friday at 1.7360/70 versus 1.7302/07 at the open and vs. 1.7285/95 at the close on Thursday.

Chartists said Friday's close above 1.7330 was very constructive for dollar/mark, set to retest 1.7423, the 1997 high. The next resistance levels are at 1.7531 and 1.7686, both highs set in February 1994.
"We'll revisit 1.7686 and go beyond that," Horner predicted. "The Germans would not mind seeing the 1.80 level, provided we do not go there too fast."
The mark's weakness was also obvious versus the yen, following Thursday's chart gap between 65.15 and 66.10.
"Mark/yen did better, but we can't rule out a retest of 65.15," one chartist at a bank said.
Renewed mark/yen weakness may prevent further strong gains on dollar/yen, wmbarked on a steady rally since meeting an objective to the downside at 110.55 Thursday in Tokyo.
"Dollar/yen may go back up to test the 116.00-118.00 area, although it is not clear how soon this would happen," Horner also said, referring to the current consolidation.
Dollar/yen ended somewhat higher at 114.80/90 vs. 114.40/50 at the open and vs. 114.15/25 at the close on Thursday.
Revisiting the 115.70 level would be key for dollar/yen's next trend because this represents an important level on a rising trendline dating back to September 1995.
Mark/Paris, which ended at 3.3780/85, is vulnerable to a retest of resistances at 3.3835 and then 3.3865, for as long uncertainty about the European Monetary Union (EMU) remains.
Merrill's Horner also said the Canadian dollar "is one of the best buys around."
The Canadian dollar is facing a series of strong levels in the area between C$1.3735 and C$1.3715, the latter being a very big level, chartists said.
